claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation or sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventional high-temperature preparation of single-phase ZrB2 tends to produce coarse grains.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has significant or relatively high residual porosity.
Porosity in conventional ZrB2 compromises structural integrity during exposure to liquid plating baths.
A liquid-phase precursor route can produce ultrafine or nanostructured diboride powder.
The liquid-phase precursor route can produce high-entropy diboride powders at 1800 °C.
Liquid-phase precursor processing will allow single-phase ZrB2 ceramic to be sintered at approximately 1800 °C.
Molecular-level precursor mixing will yield a uniformly mixed ZrB2 microstructure.
Liquid-phase precursor processing decreases diffusion distances during ZrB2 sintering.
Liquid-phase precursor processing decreases the activation energy required for ZrB2 sintering.
Shorter diffusion distances and lower activation energy increase reactivity and promote ZrB2 densification at lower temperature.
The precursor-derived ZrB2 will have lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The precursor-derived ZrB2 will have improved mechanical integrity or strength compared with conventionally sintered ZrB2.
A denser microstructure with fewer defects will better resist hole formation during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Precursor-derived ZrB2 will show better long-duration resistance to surface degradation and related failure in a liquid plating bath.
The cited high-entropy diboride results are analogous evidence suggesting feasibility for single-phase ZrB2.
Optimal processing parameters and long-term plating-bath behavior of liquid-phase-precursor-derived ZrB2 remain unestablished.
